system_description.narrative_title: Fragile Multipolar Order: Markets, Energy and Military Flashpoints
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system under stress from simultaneous economic, technological and military shocks. Rising bond yields, shifting safe-havens and active central-bank interventions coexist with energy-supply disruption from new Middle East maritime and regional conflicts, while great-power competition over technology, trade and influence amplifies fragmentation and domestic political volatility in advanced democracies. These dynamics interact non-linearly, creating feedbacks that transmit shock across finance, supply chains and security environments.
system_description.scope: States and major non-state actors, global financial markets and central banks, energy and commodity flows, maritime trade routes and ports, strategic supply chains (chips, batteries, rare earths), major regional security theatres (Middle East, Europe, East Asia), and the international institutions and rules that bind them.
system_description.super_system: The broader global political-economic-ecological system (the international order of states, markets, and planetary resource constraints).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and monetary system
Technological-industrial supply chains (semiconductors, batteries, rare earths)
Regional security complexes (Middle East, Europe, East Asia)

variables.name: Middle East maritime and energy conflict
variables.description: The U.S., Iran and regional proxies (notably Houthi forces and Gulf states) are engaged in an escalating campaign of strikes, sanctions and maritime threats that is shifting control and risk around key shipping chokepoints and global energy flows.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with sustained Western military and economic support for Kyiv, remain in a protracted high‑intensity war whose shifting frontlines, strikes on infrastructure and episodic diplomacy are reshaping European security dynamics.

variables.name: US–China technology and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are intensifying competition over advanced technology, chips, AI and strategic trade through export controls, industrial policy and reciprocal market measures, restructuring global supply chains and standards.

variables.name: Global monetary and market repricing
variables.description: Major central banks, sovereign funds and portfolio managers are undergoing a sustained repricing as higher yields, reserve reallocations, currency interventions and liquidity management are altering capital flows, reserve compositions and policy space worldwide.

variables.name: European political realignment
variables.description: A surge of far‑right and populist electoral gains across Europe is reconfiguring governing coalitions and EU policy consensus on migration, defence and economic integration, shifting the continent's internal balance and external posture.
